 BMKG Forecasts Peak Rainy Season December to February, Beware of Floods and Landslides 
 09 November 2026, 23:00 | Editorial Team 
 Tim VOI 
 Reporter 
 Edy Suherli 
 Editor 
 Head of BMKG Teuku Faisal Fathani 
 Share:
 JAKARTA - The Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) estimates that the peak of the rainy season in Indonesia lasts for three months, from December 2026 to February 2027. Although the rainfall is generally predicted to be normal, the threat of floods and landslides still needs to be considered.
 Head of BMKG Teuku Faisal Fathani said the start of the rainy season this year was 20 to 30 days behind the usual pattern. Most of Indonesia is expected to enter the rainy season only in November and December.
 "We know that most of Indonesia enters the rainy season in November and December. Then the entry of the rainy season this year is 20 to 30 days behind," said Faisal after a meeting with President Prabowo Subianto at the Presidential Palace Complex, Jakarta, Monday, November 9.
 According to Faisal, the peak of the rainy season will take place in December 2026, January, and February 2027.
 BMKG estimates that rainfall in general is in the normal category. This means that the amount of rain is not much different from the average over the past 30 years. However, this rainy season is expected to last shorter.
 This condition still requires vigilance, especially against heavy rain that can trigger floods and landslides.
 In a meeting with the President, the government discussed anticipation of wet hydrometeorological disasters, namely disasters related to weather and water conditions, such as floods and landslides due to extreme rain.
 Faisal said the BMKG had prepared an early warning system that could be accessed by the public and local governments.
 The information includes the potential for extreme rainfall, tropical cyclones, flash floods or floods due to high tides, to earthquakes and tsunamis.
 For rain, BMKG provides forecasts for the next three to six hours which are called nowcasting. This information is already available down to the sub-district level, complete with alert, standby, and caution categories.
 BMKG also provides daily to seven-day forecasts, ten-day forecasts, and monthly weather conditions forecasts.
 Faisal explained that the BMKG team together with the National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) is developing the use of this information to recognize locations that are potentially prone to flooding or landslides.
 Thus, local governments can prepare steps for handling based on the areas that are estimated to be at risk.
 In addition to heavy rain, BMKG monitors the possible impact of tropical cyclones. According to Faisal, cyclone activity at the end of 2026 is expected to be more dominant in the northern hemisphere, while early 2027 shifts to the southern hemisphere.
 Indonesia is not on the main path of tropical cyclone formation like the Philippines or Japan. However, Faisal reminded that climate change makes various extreme weather events still need to be anticipated.
